we have proposed the relativistic multirank separables of the NN interaction for S and P waves.

the multirank separability of the relativistic interaction kernel of the neutron– proton system is demonstrated and a new method for a relativistic generalizations of the nonrelativistic kernels is proposed.
the relativistic multirank separability is an efficient tool for the description of the neutron– proton scattering data.

the construction of a multirank relativistic separable kernel for the neutron–protonsystem.
the construction of the relativistic multirank separables for the neutron–protons interaction and the analysis of the experimental phase shifts in the neutron–protron scattering.
the relativistic generalization (in the framework of the relativistic effective Lagrangian approach) of the nonrelativistic multiranks separable kernels of nucleon-nucleon interaction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the relativistic multirank kernels of the neutron-proton interaction are constructed for the first time and they are suitable for the description of experimental data on phase shifts and low-energy parameters.
our model provides an adequate description of the experimental data for the neutron–protron scattering in the whole energy region considered.

the relativistic multirank kernel of the nucleon–nucleon interaction proposed in the paper is a good approximation for the description of the experimental data for the elastic scattering of nucleons in the laboratory energy range up to 3GeV.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the constructed relativistic multirank separability kernels provide a good description of the experimental data for elastic scattering of the neutron– proton system in the energy range up to 3 GeV.
the multirank kernels are constructed in a relativistic way, which are in agreement with experimental data for elastic neutron–protron scattering and low-energy parameters.
the relativistic multirank kernels are proposed and the experimental data on the elastic neutron– proton scattering are described.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the multirank relativistic separable kernel can provide a reasonable description of the elastic neutron– proton scattering data in a wide energy range.
a relativistic generalisation is required to achieve a good description of experimental data.
relativistic effects in the elastic scattering of the neutron by the proton are significant and cannot be neglected.
